title: How Operators Get Paid on Sawa: Commission, Payouts and the GoAhead
excerpt: Sawa takes 10% of the selling price and charges nothing to join. How the operating agency and selling agencies are paid, in what currency, and when travellers pay.
body_html:
Prices, timetables and visiting details are a November 2026 snapshot. Check the linked official pages and your departure’s current inclusions and terms before booking.

Quick answer

Sawa takes 10% of the selling price, and there is no fee to join. Travellers pay nothing until the GoAhead, when four travellers have reserved a date. The operating agency, one of the licensed Egyptian agencies with travellers on the date, is paid its operating costs plus a fee agreed case by case. What remains is a pool, shared per traveller to the agency that sold each seat, and the operating agency earns that share on the seats it sold too. Everything is calculated in EGP and paid in EUR, on the timing set in the agency agreement. A date that never reaches four costs nobody anything.

The Egyptian Travel Agents Association provides an independent place to check agency membership.

Key facts

Fact Detail
Cost to join None. No joining fee and no listing fee
Sawa's commission 10% of the selling price
Who is paid what The operating agency: operating costs plus an agreed fee. Every agency that sold seats, the operating agency included: a share of the pool for each seat it sold
The agreed fee Set case by case for each operating agency
Currency Calculated in EGP, paid to agencies in EUR
When agencies are paid As set in the agency agreement
Who collects traveller payments Online Era, which operates Sawa Tours (registration 148500), sends a secure payment link and collects as agent for the operating agency under General Sales Agent licence 32241. Charges to travellers are in euros
When travellers pay Nothing at reservation. Day tours: a 10% deposit as soon as the date confirms at four travellers, the balance 2 days before departure. Packages and cruises: a 25% deposit, the balance 14 days before
If the date never reaches four A day-tour date has until 7 days before the tour, a package date until 30 days before. If it falls short it is cancelled and nothing was charged, so nothing is owed to anyone
Prices Fixed per traveller; the price does not move with the size of the group
Group size Four to confirm, eight at most; when a departure fills, a new independent departure opens the same day

The first question every agency asks about a new platform is about the money: when does it arrive, what does the platform take, and who holds it in between. This guide answers those questions for Egyptian operators in the order the money moves. Some of it is fixed by the way Sawa works and is stated here in full. The rest, such as the exact payment dates, is written into the agreement an agency signs, and the agreement is the contract, not this page. The guide comes from the people behind Sawa Tours (sawa.tours), the Egypt shared-departure marketplace. We have worked in Egyptian tourism since 1993.

How does Sawa pay tour operators?

Sawa pays by role. An agency can play two roles on a departure, and each is paid differently.

  • The operating agency is one of the licensed Egyptian agencies with travellers on the date, named before the deposit is due. It runs the day under its own licence. It is paid its operating costs plus an agreed fee.
  • A selling agency sells seats. For each seat it sells it earns a share of the pool.

An agency can do both: the operating agency also earns the pool share on the seats it sold itself, and a selling agency that never operates still earns on every seat it brings. Sawa takes 10% of the selling price. Nothing is paid or owed on a date that never confirms, because no traveller was charged.

The money timeline: reservation to payout

Money moves in five stages, and no traveller is charged before the second.

Stage Travellers Agencies
1. Reserving a seat Free, with no card. Nothing is charged Nothing owed, nothing promised
2. The GoAhead (four travellers) A deposit is due by payment link as soon as the date confirms: 10% on a day tour, 25% on a package The operating agency is named before the deposit is due
3. Before departure The balance is due 2 days before a day tour, or 14 days before a package A traveller who does not pay after the GoAhead is excluded and the tour keeps running for the others
4. Departure The group travels, eight at most The operating agency runs the day under its own licence
5. Settlement Nothing further The operating agency receives its costs and fee. Each agency receives its pool share for the seats it sold, on the timing set in the agency agreement

If a date does not reach four by its deadline, it is cancelled, nobody was charged, and the stages after the first never happen. The fixed price per traveller keeps the arithmetic simple: the price does not move with the size of the group.

Commission: what Sawa takes and when

Sawa takes 10% of the selling price. There is no fee to join, no listing fee and no charge on a date that never confirms. Because nothing is charged to travellers before the GoAhead, there is nothing to take commission on until a date is confirmed.

That makes the cost of trying Sawa low. An agency that joins and sells nothing pays nothing. An agency that joins and sees its dates fall short of four also pays nothing, because those dates are cancelled without a charge.

How the money divides: an illustration

The split runs in a fixed order: Sawa's 10% of the selling price, then the operating agency's costs and fee, then the pool, shared per traveller. The figures below are invented round numbers to show that order. They are not a real tour, a real rate card or a real fee.

Suppose a departure sells at EGP 2,000 per traveller and six travellers book: four through Agency A, which operates the day, and two through Agency B.

Step Illustrative amount
Revenue (6 × EGP 2,000) EGP 12,000
Sawa's 10% of the selling price EGP 1,200
Operating agency's costs plus fee (illustrative) EGP 7,800
Pool left to share EGP 3,000, or EGP 500 per traveller
Agency A (operates, sold four seats) EGP 7,800 + 4 × EGP 500 = EGP 9,800
Agency B (sold two seats) 2 × EGP 500 = EGP 1,000

The amounts are calculated in EGP and paid in EUR. A seat booked directly on Sawa, with no selling agency, sends its pool share to Online Era. For why four travellers is the usual threshold for a day to make sense at all, see break-even group size.

How the operating agency is paid

The operating agency is paid its operating costs plus a fee agreed case by case, and it also earns the pool share on every seat it sold itself. The timing of that payment is set in the agency agreement. Read that clause before you accept your first departure, and ask Sawa to confirm it in writing.

How a selling agency is paid

A selling agency earns a share of the pool for each seat it sells. The pool is what remains of a departure's revenue once Sawa's 10% and the operating agency's costs and fee are taken out, shared per traveller. Payment timing is set in the agency agreement.

Selling is the lower-commitment role: you do not need vehicles or guides for a departure to earn from it, and you can sell on any departure in the catalogue. Operating is the higher-commitment role, because you take the day on under your own licence.

Who collects the money

Sawa Tours is a marketplace operated by Online Era, registration 148500. Travellers pay by a secure payment link from Online Era (General Sales Agent licence 32241); charges are in euros. The tour itself is run by the operating agency, a licensed Egyptian travel company named before the deposit is due, and the traveller's contract is with that agency. Sawa has a founding operating partner, Capital Travel Service (licence 2179).

What happens when travellers cancel, drop out or do not pay

A confirmed date keeps running when a traveller leaves. The traveller rules are published in the terms.

  • Day tours, cancelling at least 48 hours before departure: a full refund, deposit included.
  • Day tours, cancelling less than 48 hours before departure: deposit retained (10% of the tour price).
  • Packages and cruises: 30 or more days before, no charge; 29 to 15 days, half the deposit (12.5%); 14 days or fewer, or a no-show, the deposit (25%) is kept.
  • Force majeure (riots, revolution and similar): a full refund.
  • Not paying after the GoAhead: the traveller is excluded and the tour keeps running for everyone else.

Low numbers do not cancel a confirmed date. The full traveller-side version is in how the GoAhead works.

The short version

Sawa takes 10% of the selling price and charges nothing to join. The operating agency is paid its operating costs plus an agreed fee, and every agency earns a pool share for each seat it sold. Amounts are calculated in EGP and paid in EUR, on the timing in the agency agreement. Travellers pay nothing until the GoAhead at four, so a date that never fills costs nobody anything. Read the agency agreement for the payment dates, see sawa.tours/operators, apply through the verify page, or message Sawa on WhatsApp at +20 109 284 7613.

faq.q: How does Sawa pay tour operators?
faq.a: By role. The operating agency is paid its operating costs plus an agreed fee. Every agency, the operating agency included, earns a share of the pool for each seat it sold. Sawa takes 10% of the selling price and there is no fee to join. A date that never confirms generates no payments in either direction.

faq.q: When does the operating agency get paid?
faq.a: The timing is set in the agency agreement, so it is not quoted here. Ask Sawa to confirm it in writing before you accept your first departure.
10% of the selling price. There is no fee to join and no listing fee, and nothing is charged on a date that does not confirm.

faq.q: What currency are agencies paid in?
faq.a: Payments are calculated in EGP and paid in EUR.

faq.q: What happens to the money if my departure never confirms?
faq.a: Nothing. A day-tour date has until 7 days before the tour to reach four travellers, and a package date until 30 days before. If it does not, it is cancelled. Travellers were never charged, so there is nothing to refund and nothing to pay out.

faq.q: What if a traveller cancels or does not pay?
faq.a: The date still runs. On a day tour, a traveller who cancels more than 48 hours before departure gets a full refund, including the deposit, and one who cancels less than 48 hours before means the 10% deposit is retained. A traveller who does not pay after the GoAhead is excluded, and the tour keeps running for the others.
Online Era, which operates Sawa Tours, collects payments by secure payment link as agent for the operating agency, under General Sales Agent licence 32241. The operating agency runs the tour.

faq.q: Do I need to operate departures to earn on Sawa?
faq.a: No. A selling agency earns a share of the pool for the seats it sells without operating anything. The operator of each departure is one of the licensed agencies with travellers on the date.

faq.q: What do I need to join?
faq.a: A Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities licence, ETAA registration and insurance. Newer agencies are welcome but must show references or a portfolio. We check the documents and confirm the licence with the Ministry. There is no fee to join.
